Episode 161. Return (2)
The last day of January 1803.
As he left Lafrarosa, Jin expected the endlessly expansive apricot desert to greet him as always.
He even chuckled, recalling the time he coincidentally encountered a dark flame after his first visit to Lafrarosa, or the Moein tribe he met this time upon entry.
'What... is this?'
However, the landscape that greeted Jin when he stepped out through the door with his spiritual sword was not the Mithra Desert he knew.
A wind as sticky as rancid oil was blowing.
The wind was filled with a dreadful poison, and the land and sky visible beyond were ominously pitch-black.
And the eerie, deep groans that came from all around.
'Is this the Mithra Desert...?'
It might be understandable if it were the Black Sea.
Soon, when Jin looked down at the ground, he could realize that this desolate landscape was the 'chaotically polluted' Mithra Desert.
Sparsely scattered sand was visible all over the barren land.
Even those sands, which desperately held the last remaining vitality of nature, were turbid and had changed.
"Sigh."
The Mithra Desert is originally the land of the Myungwang tribe.

The Mithra Desert, which frustrated countless adventurers who came in pursuit of myths and legends, was the land that held the Golden City of Lafrarosa until the Myungwang tribe was on the verge of extinction.
That's why Jin dreamed of the day when his and his brothers' city would shine brightly again in this desert.
Right up until he was about to step out of this door.
Jin tightened the knot on the large knapsack he carried on his back.
Inside the knapsack were the Gwangsimjangs of the Myungwang tribes who died in the past, the chaos purifier, Vahn's blood, and the blueprints of the Gold Fleet.
'Even in death, you're causing a commotion until the end, Gliek...'
He gritted his teeth recalling the horrifying king of the Black Sea.
He was also anxious.
'If the Mithra Desert is in this condition, what about the other places?'
Polluted areas.
Two and a half years ago, there were about 50 known polluted areas in the world.
Although new polluted areas were being discovered as time went on, the Mithra Desert had been intact until Jin went to Lafrarosa.
'Just as the infectious chaos erupted after Gliek's extinction, the pollution of the land was also proliferating.'
At a glance, the pollution of the desert was serious.
It wasn't just polluted with chaos, it was to the extent that it seemed like the land where Gliek's fragments directly fell.
It was not an entirely unexpected problem.
The spread of chaos is not necessarily limited to life.
However, it was a different story that huge forces, including Runcandel and Zipfel, 'could not stop' it.
'Or, the Mithra Desert might have been excluded from the purification areas. If a large number of personnel are still being deployed to purify polluted areas worldwide, it could very well be.'
You can check the state of other areas once you leave the desert.
Anyway, his first impression upon returning to Inse after three years was very unpleasant.
"Keeek!"
Suddenly, something fiercely attacked Jin's back with a growl.
Without even looking at it, Jin exploded his aura and immediately annihilated the creature.
With it as a trigger, monsters started flocking from all around, so there was no need to observe slowly.
One hundred, two hundred, three hundred, four hundred... over a thousand.
Jin quickly estimated the approximate number of monsters that had surrounded him.
But soon he gave up.
After it exceeded a thousand, it wasn't important to grasp their number.
He just needed to wipe them all out.
Sigmund slipped out of his sword sheath.
Sword of Myungwang Spirit, 9th Sword
Extermination
Soon, the pitch-black sky was dyed blue.
The aura shaped like wings that formed behind Jin emitted a dazzling radiance.
The soaring aura seemed ready to tear the black sky at any moment.
And as soon as the aura expanded, a group of monsters that were rushing in from the front ceased breathing.
They disappeared as if being incinerated by flames.
The bones and flesh of the monsters turned to ash in the aura replaced their screams, being blown somewhere.
Monsters nearby, who reflexively tried to watch the ash scatter, met their demise on the spot.
The pale blade was scattering sword energy in all directions like reflected light.
It seemed like a hail of attacks, but the countless sword energies were slaughtering the remnants of chaos without an inch of error.
The monsters seemed emotionless.
They kept rushing towards Jin even as dozens died with each light swing of his sword.
Jin did not wish for them to feel fear and flee.
If time and circumstances allowed, he wanted to eradicate all monsters that were defiling the land of his brothers.
Every second, at least dozens, and at most hundreds of monsters burst or split apart.
Typically, chaos infectees retain some semblance of their former human selves in their appearance.
All the monsters Jin was currently slaughtering were not infectees, but pure remnants of chaos.
'There are so many.'
If he had not become the Dual King, Jin wouldn't have resolved to eliminate all monsters of the desert.
His original style was to break through, escape, assess the exact scale, and search for a more efficient method.
It was necessary to eliminate the risk of exhaustion and danger while dealing with endlessly rushing monsters.
Now there was no need for that.
Despite pouring out aura and lightning like a madman, he felt as comfortable as when he was sitting quietly in meditation.
Monsters at this level could no longer threaten Jin, even if there were a million of them.
No matter how many ants there are, they can't do anything to a dragon.
'At this point, it seems like the entire world might be using the Mithra Desert as a dumping ground... Or has Kinzelo fallen? That shouldn't be the case.'
The Mithra Desert belongs to the territory of the Beastmen, and the territory of the Beastmen is currently Kinzelo's domain.
Even if the desert is deemed worthless, there is no particular reason to abandon it to this extent.
'If Kinzelo really hasn't fallen, someone will come eventually.'
With that thought, Jin momentarily stopped his sword. Among the swarm of monsters, the figure of a human appeared.
They weren't the minions of some power he predicted would detect the battle in the desert and come searching.
'Living golems!?'
Or mines.
They were twisted like the victims rescued during the Dark Magic Society's subjugation, or faceless and hairless like the mines encountered in the Wanta Ramo Forest.
Intuitively, Jin was able to realize that they were 'discarded test subjects'.
Also, if there was a difference from the living golems and mines he had seen before, it was that their bodies were all tainted by chaos.
The chaos purifier could only work on infectees before complete erosion and physical transformation occurred.
Moreover, they had already undergone experiments before being eroded by chaos, so there was absolutely nothing that Boras' purifier could do for them.
They charged at Jin just like the monsters.
While dodging them, Jin closely observed them and soon realized a shocking fact.
'There's...a certain pattern to the chaos.'
Like magic circles or rituals, the chaos adhering to the bodies of the infectees displayed a complex yet consistent pattern.
This seemed to be a part of the experiment.
The external forces were not just cleaning up infectees and contaminated areas, but also 'utilizing' them.
The test subjects were divided into two main forms.

The failure type of the master made by Kinzelo, and the failure type of the mines, which looked like a collaboration between Zipfel and the royal family. The former used psionic energy, while the latter used aura and magical power.
It was no longer surprising that the things each test subject was pursuing were of the King of the Dead and the Magic Swordsmen.
All Jin could do for them was to grant them rest as soon as possible.
Some of them might have been forcibly captured, or betrayed while dedicating loyalty to each force, resulting in their fall as test subjects.
Either way, Jin swung his sword so they could feel as little pain as possible.
It seemed they didn't even have such basic senses left anymore.
How much time had passed like this?
The number of monsters Jin had slaughtered had already well surpassed tens of thousands, and no more discarded living golems or mines were visible.
The density of the charging monsters remained the same, but Jin was still not tired.
The more he swung his sword, the more his rage grew.
Jin was hoping that a human who could question and scrutinize this terrible situation would soon appear.
And soon, a new energy that was not chaos began to be felt from beyond the dark scenery of the polluted desert.
'Finally, they're here.'
The distance was still far, about a thousand steps or more.
However, the wind of chaos wavered unstably due to the energy emitted by the newly arrived person.
'A demon, and there's only one. Is it Zephyrin, or Bianca?'
The aura pushing back the chaos held a dark energy unique to demons.
The magical energy he often felt from powerful beings of the demon world like Zephyrin and Bianca Caligo.

After detonating the released psionic energy all at once, Jin quietly waited for him. The exploded psionic energy converged back into Jin's photon heart, and the monsters nearby couldn't withstand even that and oxidized to ashes.
Eventually, the demon revealed himself in front of Jin.
It was neither Zephyrin nor Bianca. He was a male demon Jin was seeing for the first time, and as soon as he saw Jin, he let out an exclamation as if he'd seen something interesting.
"I wondered who the crazy bastard causing chaos in my playground was... You're Jin Lun Kyndell, right?"

A lavish coat with gold embroidery, jewels and gold pieces hanging everywhere, and exaggerated gestures that he probably thought were elegant. In other words, he was showcasing with his whole body that he was a noble of the demon world.
However, unlike his frivolous exterior adorned with vanity and luxury, just his standing still made the monsters in the area pause.
Then, the monsters that rushed in again turned into bloody hail at a single gesture from him.
He was a formidable being.
From the standard of strength that Jin had held until now, he certainly was.

"Black hair, handsome face, insolent eyes. That's right, Jin Lun Kyndell! I never thought I'd meet you here. Let me introduce myself formally, my name is Lanke Hallovich. I'm the firstborn of the Great Demon World's four ducal families, Hallovich. I'm the ruler and protector of the Northern Demon World and its creatures, the owner of the Tuna Mountain and Carion Mountain, and..."
"You're Kinzelo, right? Announcing your name first was a very wise decision."
Jin interrupted his words and made eye contact with Lanke.
"…As I heard, you have no manners."
Huh?
Woosh! Lanke couldn't finish his sentence.
That's because Jin, who had rushed in in an instant, landed a punch on his jaw.
"Ugh!"
"If you hadn't, you would have had to introduce yourself with a broken jaw," Jin said.
